publications.title: Air Service Hub Network Design for Express Delivery Operations
publications.abstract:
We study an air service hub network design problem that jointly optimizes hub location, service network design, and fleet (asset) management for express delivery operations. We first introduce a compact arc-based mixed-integer linear programming formulation along with valid inequalities for the problem that can be solved directly by general-purpose solvers. To solve instances of real-world scale, we reformulate the arc-based model into a route-based model and design an exact approach that combines Benders decomposition and column generation within a branch-and-bound framework. This approach is further computationally enhanced by several acceleration strategies. We conduct extensive computational experiments using instances from two widely used data sets in the hub location literature. The results show that our method delivers optimal or near-optimal solutions for real-world–scale instances and outperforms both CPLEX and a tailored branch-price-and-cut algorithm: it is more than 12 times faster on average on instances solved to optimality and keeps the optimality gap below 12% on all instances. We show the benefits of integrated optimization by comparing our solution method with a sequential decision process that treats hub location and service network design decisions separately with an average cost reduction of 34% across all instances. We also derive several important managerial insights for express delivery carriers through sensitivity analyses.
                  Funding: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China Youth Science Fund Project [Grant 72301230] and the Research Grants Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China, University Grants Committee [Grant 25223223].
                  Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2025.0528 .

publications.title: Improving the expected profit of the data-driven newsvendor problem for lognormal demand: a statistical decision-theoretic approach
publications.abstract:
Abstract
                  Data-driven inventory management faces a critical challenge: standard “plug-in” methods that substitute point estimates into optimal rules often ignore parameter uncertainty. This practice is particularly risky under heavy-tailed lognormal demand, where it leads to severe overstocking and potential financial losses due to estimation bias. To resolve this, we formulate the parametric newsvendor problem within a unified statistical decision-theoretic framework that integrates estimation and profit maximization. We derive a closed-form Adjusted Plug-in MLE (APM) and prove that it analytically dominates the classical plug-in rule. The APM order quantity coincides with the rule obtained by specializing the operational statistics framework to this case, so that, when the shape parameter is known, it is optimal among all scale-equivariant policies. What the present analysis adds is the expected profit itself: we obtain it in closed form at a fixed sample size, for the plug-in rule and for the APM rule alike, and hence the exact fraction of the full-information expected profit that no equivariant policy can recover. From a managerial perspective, the proposed method acts as a robust safeguard against optimism bias, simultaneously reducing inventory waste (e.g., food loss) and improving expected profit. Monte Carlo simulations further confirm that these dominance results hold even when the shape parameter must be estimated, offering a simple, implementable prescriptive tool for high-uncertainty environments.

publications.title: Payout Taxes Matter: The Financing R&D Mechanism
publications.abstract:
Higher taxes on corporate payouts increase the cost of financing with stock issues. As a result, corporate investments that rely on external equity financing should be particularly sensitive to payout tax rates. A large literature shows that firms rely extensively on stock issues to fund research and development (R&D), suggesting that the financing of R&D is a potentially important microlevel mechanism linking payout taxation with real corporate activity. We document a robust negative association between dividend tax rates and firm R&D investment in a broad sample of developed countries between 2000 and 2019. The negative relation between dividend taxes and R&D is concentrated in equity-dependent firms in high-R&D industries. R&D is more sensitive to dividend tax rates in countries with stock market–based financial systems. Dividend taxes are less important for investment in physical capital than for R&D. Higher dividend taxes are associated with less corporate financing with stock issues, particularly in firms with low internal cash flow. Our study highlights the importance of focusing on equity-dependent activities and firms to evaluate the real consequences of payout taxation.
                  This paper was accepted by Gustavo Manso, finance.
                  Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.03394 .

publications.title: Does FinTech Innovation Improve Traditional Banks’ Operating Efficiency and Risk? Empirical Evidence from Patent Filings
publications.abstract:
We empirically examine the link between bank-specific innovations in financial technology (FinTech) and traditional banks’ fundamentals. We propose a new measure for FinTech innovation as the textual similarity of banks’ patent filings to standard FinTech policy documents. We show that FinTech innovation implies enhanced efficiency, profitability, and operating capacity (e.g., cost management, funding and lending activity). FinTech also ameliorates banks’ risk measures, including overall risk (Z-score), the liquidity, and nonperforming loan ratios. Our heterogeneity analysis suggests that banks with stronger managerial capacity and higher labor intensity derive moderately greater benefits from FinTech innovations. Further analysis reveals that FinTech-driven lending expansions focus on unsecured and low-risk loans, with technological specializations in cloud computing. We also find supportive evidence that expanding innovation in artificial intelligence and blockchain can yield performance gains to commercial banks.
                  This paper was accepted by Kay Giesecke, finance.
                  Funding: X. Li acknowledges support by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72495151 and 72342024]. L. Fang acknowledges support by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72371126 and 72595843]. K. Zhang acknowledges support by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72473063 and W2411065].
                  Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.03691 .

publications.title: Learning Multimodal Markov Departure Time Choice
publications.abstract:
The morning commute problem is a foundational model for analyzing how individual departure time decisions collectively shape urban traffic congestion. Despite its central role in transportation policymaking, this model still leaves several real-world phenomena unexplained. A persistent challenge lies in guaranteeing stable convergence toward stationary equilibria when commuters strategically adjust their travel choices based on prior experiences. This paper proposes a generalized mean-field game framework for the day-to-day morning commute problem. In our model, commuters with heterogeneous trip lengths and desired arrival times repeatedly receive aggregate population information and adapt their daily choices of departure times and transportation modes. A multimodal bathtub model with inflow rates derived from commuters’ daily decisions captures the evolution of traffic congestion. We establish sufficient conditions for the existence of stationary mean-field equilibria (SMFE) in this stochastic game. Next, we prescribe a hierarchical policy gradient (HPG) learning algorithm for commuters who begin without prior knowledge of population attributes and sequentially optimize their departure and mode decisions. We provide theoretical guarantees of global convergence to approximate SMFE as both the planning horizon and commuter population approach infinity. This prescriptive approach is designed for forward-looking commuters with high computational capabilities in connected urban environments. Lastly, our case studies based on real-world trip data validate the relevance of Markovian travel policies and demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed HPG algorithm. Together, these analytical and numerical results advance the understanding of how learning behavior reshapes long-term traffic equilibria and reveal the evolving dynamics of urban mobility systems with emerging transportation modes.
                  Funding: This research is based upon work partially supported by the Division of Civil, Mechanical and Manufacturing Innovation [Grants 1904575, 2233057, and 2308750] and the Air Force Office of Scientific Research [Grant FA9550-25-1-0278].
                  Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2024.0831 .
